newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes rally on refinery buying spree.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes rally on refinery buying spree.

text.p: North Sea crudes rallied strongly on Tuesday with a wave of refinery buying boosting benchmark Brent and lifting the premiums for other grades, traders said.
About eight million barrels of physical crude changed hands as refiners in northwest Europe sought to take advantage of strong margins, particularly for gas oil.
"The September overhang has gone, margins are good and they know it's not going to get any cheaper," said a trader.
Dated Brent traded at Nov Brent +3 and +9 cents after a deal on Monday at parity. The seller, who has kept most of the Oct Brent so far, added one of Tuesday's dates to the collection.
The other Brent, due to load Oct 9-11, was clocked to Texaco, traders said.
Nov Brent added 51 cents to $22.77 a barrel by 1750 GMT and the prompt backwardation also steepened slightly with the Nov/Dec spread gaining three or four cents to talk at +50 cents.
Other North Sea crudes also saw healthy interest, with three cargoes each of British Forties, Norwegian Statfjord and Oseberg changing hands at higher numbers.
Forties gained two cents from a trade on Monday at Dated Brent +18 cents, while premiums for Statfjord and Oseberg were as much as 10 and seven cents firmer respectively.
Other cargoes finding homes included an Oct 20-22 Ekofisk at Dated Brent +27 cents and a late October Draugen at +30.
In the Mediterranean, Urals tightness prompted sellers to seek a 10-cent premium on October barrels, offering Dated Brent -65 cents against Monday's deal at Dated -75 cif Italy.
With the National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) claiming to be sold out until late in October, even buyers were prepared to value Urals at Dated Brent -70 cents.
"This time they (NIOC) must be almost right because we are trying to negotiate some barrels with them without success," said a Med refiner. -- Mark Thompson, London +44 171 542 7930
